svg.title: The context encoder
svg.desc: For an event from host A (the sender of the first packet) to host B, the context encoder builds 67 event features: h from the flow encoder (32), the time since A and since B last appeared (16 each) and three port and direction features. It reads the memory of link A to B and of link B to A (100 numbers each) and turns the 267 numbers into a query. Keys come from up to 20 neighbour events: The latest event with each recent distinct peer of A and of B, excluding earlier A to B events, each described by its features and how long ago it happened, plus whether A launched it or B received it. Two-head attention combines them; The query and the attended vector give s, 100 numbers. After each batch of 512 events, messages update link memories through a GRU. The context encoder is trained to tell the real link from a fake one on benign events.
